These debug statements cluttered the CLI output during agent thinking block rendering and multiline input cursor/scroll operations. Cleanup ensures internal state changes do not emit noise to the user.

eli5.text: The command-line assistant stopped printing stray debug messages that were cluttering your terminal while it was thinking or while you were typing multi-line input. You don't need to do anything to see the difference: the next time you use the CLI, those extra log lines will simply be gone. This is a behind-the-scenes cleanup, removing leftover logging calls, so routine operations like scrolling or waiting on a thinking block no longer produce noisy output. The change is already live.

eli5.text: When you run the coding assistant from your terminal, any text that shows the program's name will now display the new name instead of the old one you may have seen in past commands or help messages. This is purely a branding update: no features changed, only the label the program reports about itself.

ai.title: Show CLI header when no local agents
ai.summary: CLI app.tsx renders header when loadedAgentsData null. Repo root uses getProjectRoot() not agentsDir dirname. Agent list and count conditional on sortedAgents existence.

eli5.text: When you open the assistant and it finds no local helper projects set up in your current folder, it now shows you a small header banner at the top instead of leaving that space blank. The banner displays the name of the project folder it searched (or your home-directory path) and a line that says how many local helpers it found, which for the none-found case reads something like "0 local agents". This affects anyone running the assistant from a directory that has no local agent files configured, and you'd notice the top of your screen now shows this information rather than being empty.

ai.title: CLI release bumped to 1.0.516
ai.summary: Version 1.0.516 increments the codebuff CLI binary version in cli/release/package.json from 1.0.515. The bump packages the preceding day's user-facing work, including multiline input cursor/layout fixes, removal of stray debug logging, the codecane-to-codebuff program name change, and header rendering when no local agents are detected.
ai.evidence: The diff for cli/release/package.json shows a one-line version bump from 1.0.515 to 1.0.516, incrementing the version field in the codebuff release package manifest.

eli5.text: This release improves the stability and polish of the CodeBuff command-line tool. It fixes how the text cursor moves and displays when you write multiple lines of input, so typing stays smooth and predictable. Stray diagnostic messages that previously appeared in your output have been cleaned up, making your interactions clearer. The tool's identity is now consistently reported as CodeBuff, so help screens and version checks show the correct name. Finally, the application now shows its header screen even when no local agents are loaded, giving you a better starting point and more informative status when opening the tool.

ai.title: CLI: findGitRoot returns null, getProjectRoot falls back to cwd
ai.summary: findGitRoot now returns null when no .git directory is found, instead of silently returning process.cwd(). getProjectRoot applies the fallback (findGitRoot() ?? process.cwd()), so callers that need a concrete path use getProjectRoot(). codebuff-client.ts switches from findGitRoot to getProjectRoot, aligning cwd resolution with the project-files module. Scope: cli/src/utils/git.ts, cli/src/project-files.ts, cli/src/utils/codebuff-client.ts.

eli5.text: When the tool looks for the folder your project lives in, it now stops searching and admits it couldn't find one instead of pretending the folder where you launched it is the answer. Only the project-files helper now silently falls back to the folder you launched the tool from when that happens. The main assistant connection uses the fallback too, so your chat session still knows which folder to work in, you won't notice a difference unless you run the tool outside any project folder, in which case it now behaves consistently instead of guessing.

ai.title: findGitRoot accepts cwd param
ai.summary: findGitRoot now takes { cwd?: string } instead of reading process.cwd() internally. Callers in project-files.ts pass cwd explicitly. Refactor only.

eli5.text: The CLI now figures out where your project lives by checking the folder you are currently in, rather than guessing from a hidden default. If you open the assistant inside a subfolder of a Git project, it will look upward from that exact folder instead of relying on a built-in fallback, which prevents it from landing in the wrong place. This is just an internal tidy-up: the behavior you see hasn't changed, but the way it finds your project is now more explicit and less likely to guess wrong.
